first_impression.reaction: I Googled centrepieces because the florist quotes are where I expect the padding to be. I went straight to the FAQ and 'Where the money goes'. The FAQ is short and plain, no 'your love story' stuff. The money section gives me levers but not a single number, and it sends me off to another article for the bill. Fine for a style guide. I skimmed the 30 ideas, read the practical bits and the venue questions properly, which are actually useful.

journey.quote: The piece that stops you scrolling was styled for one room, one table shape and one light.
journey.reaction: Fair point, and honest. It admits the Pinterest photo probably won't work on our tables. That's a limitation stated up front, which I respect.

journey.quote: Make them in this order and the right look usually chooses itself.
journey.reaction: No it doesn't. Four decisions narrow things down, sure, but 'chooses itself' is filler.

journey.quote: Stems are the expensive part of most arrangements, so the levers are about using fewer of them well:
journey.reaction: Practical. Reusing ceremony flowers and padding with greenery are things I can actually push the florist on. No numbers, but it doesn't pretend to have any either, and it links out to a cost article.

journey.quote: If you would rather talk the choices through than decide alone, our [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-centrepieces&utm_content=primary) team can help you brief the tables.
journey.reaction: A sales link before I've seen any of the 30 ideas. Sitting right inside the money section makes me wonder whether the 'help' comes with a florist you get a cut from.

journey.quote: [General candle safety guidance](https://www.mfs.sa.gov.au/community-safety/safety-and-education/fact-sheets/candles2/mfs-fact-sheet-candles.pdf) also calls for sturdy holders that will not tip over, made of material that cannot burn.
journey.reaction: A real source, a fire service fact sheet, not 'experts say'. That's the kind of thing I'd click and check, and it would hold up.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so these details are settled before anything is booked.
journey.reaction: Best line on the page for me. In writing, before I commit. My last vendor problem was exactly a verbal 'that's included'. Doesn't tell me what you charge, but it's a concrete promise.

journey.quote: Do you allow open flame, and do candles need to sit in glass?
journey.reaction: A checklist I can paste into an email to a venue. Useful whether I use you or not, which makes me trust it more.

journey.section: Planning the table with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, start to finish.
journey.reaction: 'Payments' is the word I stop on. Do the payments to the florist and venue go through you? If so, is there a margin on them? The page doesn't say, and 'start to finish' is brochure talk.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Advisor paid: flat fee, percentage, or commission from venues and florists?
If payments to suppliers go through you, are supplier prices marked up?
When the Wedded Concierge helps 'brief the tables', do you recommend florists you have a commercial arrangement with?
What does a centrepiece actually cost per table? Is there a real wedding with the actual floral budget I can look at?
What exact height counts as 'low enough to talk over'? (The page defers this to the table decor guide.)

turn_offs_found.quote: If you would rather talk the choices through than decide alone, our [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-centrepieces&utm_content=primary) team can help you brief the tables.
turn_offs_found.why: CTA before the evidence. The 30 ideas and the useful checklists come after it.

turn_offs_found.quote: Make them in this order and the right look usually chooses itself.
turn_offs_found.why: A promise with nothing behind it. Small, but it's the kind of line that makes me read the rest more suspiciously.

would_share_with: My fiancee, mainly for the venue and florist question lists

cta_reaction.quote: Begin the conversation with our [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-centrepieces&utm_content=closing) team.
cta_reaction.why: The closing CTA at least comes after the useful material, and 'confirms inclusions in writing' earned some credit. I might click to see what the Concierge page says about fees. I wouldn't enquire until I know whether you take a cut from suppliers, and this page doesn't tell me.

top_3_changes: In the closing section, replace the vague 'start to finish' with the written-inclusions promise the page already makes. Old: "One Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, start to finish." New: "One Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit."

Take the sales link out of the money section so it isn't the first CTA before any ideas. Old: "If you would rather talk the choices through than decide alone, our [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-centrepieces&utm_content=primary) team can help you brief the tables." New: "" (delete; the secondary and closing CTAs remain, after the evidence). If CRO needs a primary CTA, move this sentence to just after "Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so these details are settled before anything is booked." instead.
Cut the overpromise in How to choose. Old: "Make them in this order and the right look usually chooses itself." New: "Make them in this order and the shortlist gets much shorter."

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
No invented brand facts; fee model, commissions and supplier sourcing listed as unanswered, not assumed
Suggested edits use exact old/new strings and add no new facts or measurements
HTML comments, fact markers and image slots treated as invisible

open_questions.question: Deleting the primary mid-article CTA may conflict with CRO placement rules; is moving it below the Practical details 'in writing' line acceptable instead?

assumptions: Daniel searched 'wedding centrepieces' to understand where floral costs come from while comparing planners, so his relevance score is low for a style-led post.
Fees, commissions and supplier sourcing are deferred by the brand, so no edit proposes stating them; they remain as unanswered questions only.
